summary: The behaviour this item promises is real: at dda45bf the stage composes with the real publisher, installs all seven composed packs with each pack's own scaffolder, every adopter gate exits zero, the full gate is GREEN with 'packaging: pass' inside it, and an independent recursive snapshot of the whole tree plus $HOME before and after a run showed not one byte written outside the temporary directory. The failure is in the EVIDENCE, which is this project's dominant defect class. Two of the five criteria do not assert their own headline property, and in both cases I drove the falsification the spec itself declares and the row it names stayed green. AC4 is the worse one: writing into $HOME on every call, writing into the repository at git-ignored paths (including .veldo/trackers.json, the one file the ignore rule exists to protect), and detaching every child process into its own session each left the suite at 47 passed / 0 failed, because the assertion is `git status --porcelain` equality plus an AST identifier scan rather than an observation of what was written. AC1 is the same shape at the item's centre: nothing records WHICH scaffolder executed, so pointing the installer at this repository's own .veldo/init_scaffold.py left all three AC1 rows green and the stage printed 'install-and-run: pass' with '(engine/ present: False)' on all seven packs while every install had in fact been laid from engine/. Both properties hold in today's code; nothing would notice if they stopped. Fixes are small and mechanical: record the scaffolder path actually executed and assert it is under the pack, and replace the git-status proxy with a recursive inventory of the repository plus the process's declared write roots. TWO THINGS THE READER OF THIS FILE MUST KNOW. First, writing this artifact reds the gate: WARP-0727 AC1 asserts the git-tracked verdict domain equals the on-disk corpus, so an uncommitted verdict makes the unit stage fail until it is committed, even though the corpus owner's own divergence report calls the same path legitimately untracked (F10). Second, the L2 template's findings vocabulary (blocker, major, minor) is rejected by .veldo/validate.py, which requires blocking or note, so every entry below carries the legal severity plus the template's value in l2_severity (F9). Nothing in this file was written into the reviewed repository other than this file itself; all mutation testing ran in a scratch copy.

criteria.note: DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION LITERALLY and the named row did not red. Mutated install_and_run to run `ROOT / SCAFFOLDER` instead of `pack_dir / SCAFFOLDER` (diff proven), which is exactly 'point the installer at this repository's own .veldo/init_scaffold.py instead of the COMPOSED pack's copy'. Result: 45 passed / 2 failed, and BOTH reds were AC3 teeth rows; every AC1 row stayed green. `python3 scripts/check_install_and_run.py` under the mutation printed 'install-and-run: pass' and, for all seven packs, 'installed 82 file(s) from /tmp/.../packs/<pack> (engine/ present: False) -> adopter gate GREEN' - a provenance claim that was false, since .veldo/init_scaffold.py line 39 sets DEFAULT_TEMPLATES = ROOT/'engine' when that directory exists, so every install was laid from engine/. Root cause: install_and_run records `installed_from` = the pack directory it was HANDED and `pack_has_engine_dir` computed from that same directory; the scaffolder path actually executed is never recorded, so the suite row whose prose says 'the scaffolder that ran is the PACK'S OWN copy, asserted by the path each result records' asserts no such thing. WHAT I DID CONFIRM: in the unmutated tree the pack's own scaffolder is what runs, all seven composed packs genuinely have no engine/ directory, and the negative control (this repository does have engine/) is true. The property is true today and unasserted; the mutation is caught only incidentally by AC3, and only because a corrupted pack stops biting once the pack is no longer the template source.

TEETH ON BOTH READINGS OF THE FALSIFICATION. (a) Replaced the derived set: `report['composed'] = ['claude']` -> 44 passed / 3 failed, reddening the AC2 set-equality row, the guard's teeth row and the guard's negative control. (b) Replaced the install list only, keeping `composed` derived: `wanted = ['claude']` -> 46 passed / 1 failed, reddening the set-equality row alone, which proves SET EQUALITY itself has teeth and not merely the `len(composed) >= 2` clause. Also read and accepted the vacuous-run guard: the injected `_iar_empty` composer produces a tree with no composed pack and the stage fails by name with NO_PACKS_COMPOSED (rep['results'] == [] and the name appears in report_lines), driven through the composer seam rather than asserted about it, and the default composer produces 7 packs as the negative control. Failure taxonomy is asserted as exactly the four declared names with no duplicate spelling.

THE EXIT-ZERO ASSERTION HAS TEETH, WITH TWO CAVEATS I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN WAIVING. Drove 'ignore the nested gate's exit status': deleted `if g.returncode != 0: out['failure'] = FAIL_GATE` (diff proven) -> 46 passed / 1 failed, reddening 'AC3 THE GATE'S OWN TEETH' (the invalid-STARTER.md row). CAVEAT 1: the row the spec's falsified_by names - the corrupted required substrate file - stayed GREEN under that mutation, because that corruption breaks init before the gate is ever consulted; the suite's own comment admits this, so the spec text is stale relative to the suite that carries the teeth (finding F6). CAVEAT 2: what 'their gate went green' covers is far narrower than the prose reads. I ran a scaffolded pack by hand: its catalog is 'catalog: 1 run, 22 not-applicable', the single required item is scripts/secret_inventory.py, and because the stage runs `git init` but never commits or stages, that check enumerates via `git ls-files` and reports '0 scanned' - a confident zero. The green also contains two recorded stand-downs (release check, shape gate) and 'GATE: GREEN (no-git)'. What is genuinely proven green is the built-in veldo contracts validation, which does bite - that is the check the STARTER.md mutation trips (finding F3).

THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION LEAVES THE SUITE ENTIRELY GREEN, THREE WAYS. The criterion says 'every byte of it lands under a temporary directory' and 'it makes no network call and starts no detached process'; the assertions are `git status --porcelain` string equality on this repository plus an AST identifier scan of one file. (a) Added `(Path.home()/'.veldo-l2-outside-probe').write_text(...)` to check() -> 47 passed / 0 failed, and the file was on disk afterwards. (b) Added writes to `.veldo/trackers.json` and `scripts/__pycache__/l2probe.txt` INSIDE the repository under check -> 47 passed / 0 failed, `git status --porcelain` empty, and .veldo/trackers.json clobbered - the per-org tracker config the .gitignore exists to keep out of commits, hence the one file in the tree git could not restore. (c) Added `start_new_session=True` to the single subprocess helper, detaching every child into its own session -> 47 passed / 0 failed, because the AST walk collects Name.id and Attribute.attr and never sees a keyword argument. WHAT IS EVIDENCED: the 'temporary directory is REMOVED' half has teeth (deleting the rmtree reds two rows), and the identifier scan does catch the six spellings it lists. WHAT I CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, so the property is true today: a recursive inventory of all 1529 files (path, size, mtime) before and after a run, plus a listing of $HOME, was byte-identical, and neither scripts/publish.py nor the nested gate contains any network call. Nothing asserts it.

REGISTRATION IS REAL AND UNCONDITIONAL. scripts/verify.sh:36 reads CHECK_packaging="required:python3 scripts/check_install_and_run.py", and a full `bash scripts/verify.sh` in my scratch copy printed the seven per-pack lines then 'packaging: pass' and ended GATE: GREEN at dda45bff3e86, so the stage runs on every gate run rather than when somebody remembers. Drove both declared falsifications: rewriting the slot as `na:` reds one AC5 row, and naming the script inside an `na:` reason without requiring it reds two (declared != required). The 'deliberately absent from the shipped template' row and the executable-as-a-subprocess row both pass as written. Two notes: that absence row is a substring scan, so a truthful `na:not packaged (... scripts/check_install_and_run.py ... does not ship here)` reason in engine/scripts/verify.sh reds this repository's gate - I drove it, 46 passed / 1 failed (F7); and both capability manifests still carry the pre-approval sentence 'NOT YET A CATALOG ITEM ... so AC5 REPORTS until that lands and REFUSES after', which is false at this commit (F5).

findings.text: AC4's headline property - 'IT TOUCHES NOTHING OUTSIDE A TEMPORARY DIRECTORY' - cannot fail. The check is `git status --porcelain` equality on this repository, which is blind to (i) every path outside the repository and (ii) every git-ignored path inside it, and the companion claim 'starts no detached process' is an AST scan over Name/Attribute identifiers, which is blind to keyword arguments. Three mutations that the spec's own falsified_by field describes ('make scripts/check_install_and_run.py write anywhere outside its temporary directory') each left the suite at 47 passed / 0 failed. FIX: replace the proxy with an observation - a recursive inventory (path, size, digest) of the repository root plus an explicit assertion that the only mutated prefix is the mkdtemp path, and assert the subprocess call's own kwargs rather than scanning identifiers.
findings.evidence: Mutation (a) into $HOME: diff `+ (Path.home() / '.veldo-l2-outside-probe').write_text('this byte did not land in a temp dir')` in check(); `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 24_veldo_0007_install_and_run` -> 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 47 passed, 0 failed in 4.52s'; `ls -l ~/.veldo-l2-outside-probe` -> a 37 byte file owned by dmitry, timestamped 07:21, whose contents are the probe string. Mutation (b) into ignored paths in the repo under check: diff writes `.veldo/trackers.json` and `scripts/__pycache__/l2probe.txt` -> 47 passed, 0 failed; `git status --porcelain` empty; `cat .veldo/trackers.json` -> '{"l2": "clobbered"}'. Mutation (c) detached children: diff `+ start_new_session=True,` in _run -> 47 passed, 0 failed. All three in a scratch copy at /tmp/.../scratchpad/rev-VELDO-0007, each restored with `git checkout -- .` and the suite re-run green.

findings.text: AC1 - the criterion the spec calls 'THE ENTIRE POINT' - has no assertion that distinguishes the composed pack's scaffolder from this repository's. install_and_run records the pack directory it was handed (`installed_from`) and `pack_has_engine_dir` derived from that same directory; the executable actually invoked is never recorded. Pointing the installer at this repository's own scaffolder therefore leaves every AC1 row green while the stage reports, falsely, that each install came from a tree with no engine/. The 1.0 defect class (init assuming the engine/ shape) is caught here only by luck, through AC3's teeth rows, and only because a corrupted pack stops biting once the pack is no longer the template source - if this repository's scaffolder ever worked from a composed pack by coincidence, AC1 would pass on a wrong install. FIX: record the scaffolder path executed in the result dict and assert it is under the composed pack root; that also makes the suite's existing prose ('asserted by the path each result records') true.
findings.evidence: Mutation: `- init = _run([sys.executable, pack_dir / SCAFFOLDER, '.'], cwd=target)` / `+ init = _run([sys.executable, ROOT / SCAFFOLDER, '.'], cwd=target)`, diff shown. Suite: 45 passed, 2 failed - the two reds were 'VELDO-0007 AC3 THE TEETH' and 'VELDO-0007 AC3 THE GATE'S OWN TEETH'; `grep -o "VELDO-0007 AC[0-9][^:]*"` over the failures returned AC3 rows only. Under the same mutation `python3 scripts/check_install_and_run.py` printed 'install-and-run: pass' with all seven lines reading '(engine/ present: False) -> adopter gate GREEN' at 82 files each (81 with the pack's own scaffolder, so the trees genuinely differ). Provenance of the template source: .veldo/init_scaffold.py:39 `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES = ROOT / "engine" if (ROOT / "engine").is_dir() else ROOT`.

findings.text: The adopter gate that AC3 requires to be green runs one of twenty-three catalog slots, and that one required check inspects zero files. The stage runs `git init` in the fresh tree and never commits or stages, so scripts/secret_inventory.py - the only `required:` slot in the shipped catalog - enumerates through `git ls-files` and finds nothing: it reports '0 scanned' and its posture is advisory (reporting, not blocking) anyway. The green also contains two stand-downs recorded as pass (release check, shape gate) and is labelled 'GATE: GREEN (no-git)'. So 'the adopter's own gate went green' is, in substance, the built-in veldo contracts validation plus a zero-file scan. That built-in does bite, which is why the item is not vacuous - but the sentence reads like a full gate and is not one. FIX: `git add -A && git commit -m init` in the scaffolded tree before running its gate, which is also what a real adopter's first ten minutes look like, and the one required check then actually scans the 59 files init laid down.
findings.evidence: Ran install_and_run by hand into /tmp/l2-probe-*/fresh and printed gate_tail: '== security / secret inventory: 0 outstanding (0 exposed in reachable history), 0 dispositioned, 0 advisory, 0 scanned; posture=advisory (reporting, not blocking)' ... 'release check STANDS DOWN, recorded rather than passed: no releases directory at all' ... 'shape gate: no architecture contract, standing down (adoption safe)' ... 'catalog: 1 run, 22 not-applicable (reasons on record), 0 waived, 0 undeclared' ... 'GATE: GREEN (no-git)'. In that tree `git ls-files | wc -l` -> 0, and scripts/secret_inventory.py:44 enumerates with `_git(root, 'ls-files', '-z')`. `grep -n '^CHECK_' scripts/verify.sh` in the scaffolded repo: 22 na, 1 required (security).

findings.text: VELDO_NO_NETWORK=1 is set into every child process's environment by scripts/check_install_and_run.py and is read by nothing in this repository. It reads as a network kill-switch protecting the nested compose-install-gate path and executes nothing; the actual no-network property rests entirely on the AST scan of one file, which says nothing about scripts/publish.py or the nested gate. I verified by hand that neither of those makes a network call, so the property holds - but the control that appears to enforce it is inert prose in code form.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "VELDO_NO_NETWORK" --include=*.py --include=*.sh --include=*.md .` over the whole tree (excluding proof/) returns exactly one hit: scripts/check_install_and_run.py:76, its own definition. `grep -n "urlopen|requests|push|ls-remote|http|socket|curl|Popen" scripts/publish.py` returns only a prose line in its docstring; the same grep over engine/scripts/verify.sh returns nothing.

findings.text: Both capability manifests still describe the pre-approval world, and one of them ships. .veldo/capabilities.yaml and engine/.veldo/capabilities.yaml carry, for install_and_run_smoke, the sentence 'NOT YET A CATALOG ITEM: declaring the slot edits scripts/verify.sh, a protected path needing a recorded approval, so AC5 REPORTS until that lands and REFUSES after' - false at this commit, where the slot is `required:` and AC5 is unconditional with its reporting branch deliberately removed. Separately, AC5's claim 'IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE SHIPPED TEMPLATE' is asserted only against engine/scripts/verify.sh, while the shipped template does carry the repo-only script's path: engine/.veldo/capabilities.yaml declares home: scripts/check_install_and_run.py, and the scaffolder lays that manifest into every adopter tree as .veldo/capabilities.yaml, where the named file does not exist. `scope: repo-only` is what keeps that honest, and nothing asserts the scope marker.
findings.evidence: `grep -n install_and_run .veldo/capabilities.yaml` and `grep -n install_and_run engine/.veldo/capabilities.yaml` both return line 187 containing 'NOT YET A CATALOG ITEM ... AC5 REPORTS until that lands and REFUSES after' alongside 'scope: repo-only'; scripts/verify.sh:36 is `CHECK_packaging="required:python3 scripts/check_install_and_run.py"`. In a scaffolded tree, `grep -c check_install_and_run .veldo/capabilities.yaml` -> 1 while the file scripts/check_install_and_run.py is absent.

findings.text: AC3's falsified_by names a row that does not red. It says the assertion is 'driven by breaking a required substrate file in the composed pack', but under the mutation it prescribes (ignore the nested gate's exit status) the corrupted-substrate row stays green - that corruption breaks init, so the failure is INIT_FAILED and the row accepts either name. The row with the teeth is the invalid-STARTER.md one, which the suite added after finding the first vacuous and says so in its comment. The spec's own falsification text was not updated to match, so a reader driving the spec as written would conclude the criterion is vacuous when it is not.
findings.evidence: Mutation deleting `if g.returncode != 0: out['failure'] = FAIL_GATE` -> 46 passed, 1 failed, the single red being 'VELDO-0007 AC3 THE GATE'S OWN TEETH'. The substrate row ('AC3 THE TEETH ... with a required substrate file CORRUPTED') stayed green. Suite comment at that row: 'FOUND VACUOUS BY DRIVING: the row above accepts INIT_FAILED or ADOPTER_GATE_RED, so disabling the gate-status check entirely left the suite green'.

findings.text: AC5 proves an absence with a substring scan, so documenting the exclusion reds the gate. The row asserts the string 'scripts/check_install_and_run.py' does not appear anywhere in engine/scripts/verify.sh. Writing the true reason into the shipped template's na: slot - the natural way to record why the slot is not applicable to an adopter - therefore reddens this repository's gate. 'Mentioning equals requiring' is the right rule for THIS repository's gate; in the shipped template a comment is not a registration.
findings.evidence: Mutation: `CHECK_packaging="na:not packaged"` -> `CHECK_packaging="na:not packaged (veldo home only: scripts/check_install_and_run.py composes packs and does not ship here)"` in engine/scripts/verify.sh; suite -> 46 passed, 1 failed with an AC5 row red.

findings.text: AC4's 'a sweep of runs cannot fill the disk' row only observes a run that returns normally. shutil.rmtree sits in a `finally`, which a killed process skips, and there were 302MB of leftover /tmp/veldo-install-and-run-* trees on this machine before my session began - eleven of them, in three groups whose timestamps match three prior suite runs (05:12, 05:13 and 07:01, the last matching the producer's own driven-falsifications re-run at 11:00:30Z / 07:00 EDT). I could not reproduce a leftover from a run that completes: my CLI run and my suite runs each cleaned up, and the leftovers contain no read-only directory that would defeat rmtree, so the cause is a process that did not reach its finally rather than a bug in the cleanup itself. Worth knowing because the row is stated as a disk-safety property and the failure mode it would need to catch is exactly the interrupted run.
findings.evidence: `du -sch /tmp/veldo-install-and-run-*` -> '302M total' with `ls -d ... | wc -l` -> 11, all with mtimes 05:12-07:01 predating this review; `find <leftover> -type d ! -perm -u+w` -> empty. Removing the rmtree line does red two AC4 rows (45 passed, 2 failed), so the happy-path assertion works. I deleted only the directories my own runs created and left the eleven pre-existing ones untouched.

findings.text: Adjacent to the subject but load-bearing for this review's own artifact: the criteria-coverage rule that the L2 brief calls gate-enforced is not applied to verdicts. .veldo/validate.py:864 calls check_criteria_coverage only for proof MANIFESTS; the verdict corpus at line 867 gets check_json(VERDICT_REQ) alone, so a verdict that omits a criterion, invents one, or duplicates one passes the gate. What the gate DOES enforce on a verdict is a findings vocabulary the L2 template contradicts: list-shaped entries must carry severity blocking|note, so writing the template's blocker|major|minor verbatim reds the contracts stage. This file therefore uses blocking|note as validate.py requires and carries the L2 severity beside it in l2_severity.
findings.evidence: Wrote a probe verdict with severity 'blocker' into a scratch copy: `python3 .veldo/validate.py all` -> exit 1 with 'proof/VELDO-0007/verdict-l2.json: list-shaped findings entries need severity blocking|note and text'; changing the one value to 'blocking' -> exit 0. `sed -n 855,875p .veldo/validate.py` shows check_criteria_coverage called under MANIFEST_PATTERN only.

findings.text: OUTSIDE THIS ITEM'S FOOTPRINT, FOUND BY USING THE FEATURE: writing this very verdict artifact turns the gate RED, and it stays red until the file is committed. scripts/suites/13_warp_0623_codified_live.py:2574 (WARP-0727 AC1) asserts, over the LIVE repository, that the git-tracked verdict domain EQUALS the on-disk validated corpus. An uncommitted verdict artifact is on disk and not in the index, so the sets differ by exactly one and the unit stage fails. The corpus owner disagrees with its own guard: .veldo/verdict_corpus.divergence classifies my file as `untracked` and leaves entitled_not_validated, contradiction, overclaimed and misfiled all EMPTY, and validate_checks documents in words that 'UNTRACKED is the one legitimate reason and is expected (an author validating before committing), so it is not red'. The suite's extra equality clause reds it anyway. This is the shape the L2 brief names: a live-state assertion requiring set equality that reddens the gate the first time somebody uses the feature, and every reviewer in this fleet trips it. FIX: compare the tracked domain against the validated corpus MINUS the untracked bucket the owner already computes, so an author validating before committing is green and a tracked/validated contradiction is still red.
findings.evidence: In a scratch copy at dda45bf: `bash scripts/verify.sh` GREEN (catalog 8 run, 15 na) with no verdict file; then with proof/VELDO-0007/verdict-l2.json present -> 'selftest: 4529 passed, 1 failed', 'unit: FAIL', 'GATE: RED (dda45bff3e86...)'. Isolated: `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 13_warp_0623_codified_live` -> 3511 passed, 1 failed with the file, 3512 passed, 0 failed after `mv` of that one file. Witness printed by calling the shipped functions directly: tracked(domain)=170, on-disk(validated)=171, validated minus domain = ['proof/VELDO-0007/verdict-l2.json'], domain minus validated = [], while verdict_corpus.divergence reports entitled_not_validated=[], contradiction=[], overclaimed=[], misfiled=[], untracked=['proof/VELDO-0007/verdict-l2.json'].
